old_problem: The exact source ties one source row to contradictory acceptance semantics. Items and Procedure select AlwaysOff and a remain-off outcome after AC restoration. Criterion 1 instead selects AlwaysOn while retaining that remain-off outcome. The same record also requires a separate physical CPU swap and later successful power-on, but supplies no authoritative policy-result pair, swap BOM, stimulus oracle or recovery contract. The preceding AlwaysOn case and following Last state case are separate identities and cannot repair this row.
disposition_reason: Retain Pending and BLOCKED. A PowerRestorePolicy name is the controlled variable, not a fillable runtime parameter: AlwaysOff and AlwaysOn normally entail opposite automatic chassis behavior after AC returns. The literal `AlwaysOn` plus `remain power-off` criterion cannot be treated as an AlwaysOff typo without changing the Master acceptance semantics. A standard Redfish/IPMI draft can only document a future interface; it cannot decide the write value or make a contradictory observed state PASS. The CPU replacement checkpoint is independently preserved but cannot make the undefined precondition or post-AC result safe. The BMC/platform owner must issue an overlay ruling that selects one policy/result pair (or two separately accepted checkpoints), the CPU-swap trigger/oracle and restoration; then this Source Key requires a fresh review.
decision_basis: The exact XLSX Functionality row 1583, matching same-row DeepSeek/test-json fields, V2 review, historical V3.1 BLOCKED record, exact-code/variant history and the locked formal queue were reread directly. The next formal identity was directly opened as row 1622 / Wistron-BMC-00893-V002 / f2599d0a0fe990d3; it was not inferred from numbering.

Items and Procedure independently name AlwaysOff, then require an AC off/on event and a remain-off observation. Criterion 1 literally names AlwaysOn with the same observation. Selecting either source branch changes both the policy write and the state-machine oracle.

For a chassis power-restore setting, an API readback proves only the configured value. It does not prove the source-required physical AC-loss/return behavior, and it cannot make an AlwaysOn/remain-off observation semantically valid.

The source requires BMC-Web interaction and visual/photos; future Redfish/IPMI evidence may corroborate the selected setting but cannot substitute for required fresh GUI/physical observation. The private Script does not supply an authoritative policy/result mapping.

The CPU9654-to-CPU9554 service step is a separate hardware configuration/boot checkpoint. It needs exact approved processor parts, socket/BIOS/AGESA compatibility, ESD/thermal procedure, de-energized service boundary, activation stimulus, POST/early-DXE/OS-ready oracle and a recovery plan; it must not be dropped or used to assume the AC policy result.

The missing result is not merely BMC address, credentials, PDU outlet or package version. Those can be runtime prerequisites after an approved acceptance rule exists; here the rule needed to interpret the write and result itself is contradictory.

ED-06 preserves AC/full-power behavior as distinct from warm/cold reboot; ED-20 requires actual WebUI/visual evidence where the source requires it; ED-29 requires observable OFF -> ON -> OS Ready when a future power-cycle completion path is selected. None licenses changing AlwaysOn to AlwaysOff.

ED-02/ED-21 retain this row's Source Key/Variant identity despite adjacent policy cases; ED-03/ED-13 allow a standard BMC draft only without invented OEM semantics; ED-17/ED-25 keep physical power and CPU work operator-controlled; ED-24 preserves the source conflict for an overlay decision; ED-26 bars automatic retry; ED-33/ED-35/ED-36/ED-38 preserve Master/coverage, distinguish review from execution and prohibit a DUT verdict.

Do not set PowerRestorePolicy in WebUI, Redfish or IPMI; do not use a guessed endpoint/payload, `curl -k`, command-line password or private Script assumption; do not AC/DC cycle, reboot, hot-pull power, swap CPUs, clear SEL/dmesg/syslog or submit a policy write. test_case.pass_fail_basis: Remain BLOCKED and Engineering Decision Pending until the owner disposes of AlwaysOff/remain-off versus AlwaysOn/remain-off, then supplies the exact accepted physical AC state transition and distinct post-CPU-swap completion rule. A future selected AC power-cycle path must evidence the required OFF -> ON -> OS Ready transitions when ON is expected; a successful API call, one ping, a generic Redfish field or a neighboring AlwaysOn/Last-state record is not a PASS basis. The eventual DUT verdict remains engineer-owned.

Do not change BMC policy, drive an AC/PDU feed, reset/reboot the host, replace a CPU or clear evidence before the engineering ruling and one explicit execution authorization for the exact selected run.
Do not hot-pull a running service; future physical AC and CPU work requires a dedicated/quiesced SUT, qualified operator, ESD/thermal controls and independent BMC/console/PDU recovery.
Do not expose credentials or disable TLS; future interface discovery and state evidence must use protected target identity and redacted logs.
Do not substitute Redfish/IPMI telemetry for source-required BMC-Web screenshots/photos or human physical AC/CPU observations.
Preserve existing SEL, audit, kernel, OS, POST and early-DXE evidence; no automatic retry, repeat cycle, reboot, policy re-write or restoration-by-assumption is authorized.
This review performs no DUT action and makes no hardware PASS, FAIL or N/A claim.
